The client header is shape-checked against /^[A-Za-z0-9._:-]{1,64}$/ and then ALWAYS hashed, so a request header can never choose an option name and the key stays inside the option_name budget.

findings.claim: files_on_disk_audit counts were wrong: counted 35 (actual 36), php 17 (actual 19), plan_scratch 4 (actual 5). Author miscount in v1.2.0.

Apollo_Waha_Options is require_once'd ONLY from the top of inc/Client/class-client.php. It works today purely because inc/class-plugin.php happens to list Client first in $files. Reorder that array — or reach Session/Admin by any path that does not load Client — and every call fatals with 'Class Apollo_Waha_Options not found'. Latent, not currently reachable: uninstall.php does not use it and boot() always loads Client first.
findings.fix: Add 'inc/class-options.php' as the FIRST entry of $files in inc/class-plugin.php and drop the guarded require from class-client.php.
findings.status: FIXED in RUN 2 (2026-09-11) — class-options.php is now the first require in the loader with a comment pinning it there, and the guarded require is gone from class-client.php.

findings.claim: Apollo_Waha_Options::mask() reveals 4 of 7 characters on short secrets: 'abcdefg' renders as 'ab***fg' (verified by running the function). Harmless for the real 48-char HMAC key or a normal API key, but the all-bullets threshold (<=6) is too low.
findings.fix: Raise the full-mask threshold to <=12, or always reveal at most the final 2 characters.

findings.claim: Apollo_Waha_Options::set() passes autoload=false for the two secrets, but on WordPress < 6.6 update_option() ignores the autoload argument when the option ALREADY exists. A secret written before this code shipped could remain autoload=yes.
findings.fix: For secrets, delete_option() then add_option($k,$v,'',false) on first write, or require WP >= 6.6.
findings.status: OPEN — does not affect fresh installs

findings.claim: apollo_wa_last_ping autoloads (only the two SECRET_KEYS are forced false) yet is written on every ping cache miss and read on one admin screen.
findings.fix: Add it to a NON_AUTOLOAD list alongside the secrets.

findings.claim: apollo_wa_base_url is admin-settable and flows unvalidated into wp_remote_request — no scheme or host allowlist. Gated behind manage_options so it is an admin-can-do-admin-things issue, BUT security.media_fetch_allowlist already declares 'waha base host only + X-Api-Key' as the intent, so the declared control is not implemented.
findings.fix: Validate scheme is http/https and, for media fetches later, pin the host to the configured base URL host.

findings.claim: admin/views/settings.php reads $_GET['updated'] with isset() and no sanitisation/nonce. The value is never echoed, so it is not an injection, but any admin can trigger the success notice with &updated=1 and WPCS will flag the unslashed superglobal.
